memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away. - Gen 15:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A small verse, easily overlooked. Abram has laid out the sacrifice, and now he waits. And while he waits, vultures circle down, trying to snatch away what he has prepared. So Abram stands there in the heat, driving them off. Waiting for God, swatting at birds.

There is something deeply true here about the life of faith. Between God's promise and God's fulfilment there is often a waiting - and the waiting is not peaceful. Things come to snatch away what God has given us. Doubts descend. Distractions circle. The enemy of our souls "prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour" (1 Pet 5:8).

Abram's job in that moment was simply to guard what God had asked for and refuse to let it be carried off. Not glamorous. Not miraculous. Just faithful, tiring vigilance.

Sometimes that is exactly what God asks of us - to protect what He has given while we wait for what He has promised. Guard your prayer life when it feels dry. Guard your marriage when it's under pressure. Guard your faith when doubts circle. "Be alert and of sober mind" (1 Pet 5:8). The vultures will come. Drive them away, and keep waiting on God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What is God asking you to guard while you wait on Him?
- What "birds of prey" are circling your faith right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, in the long wait between Your promise and its fulfilment, help me guard what You have given me. Make me alert and faithful, driving away what would snatch away my trust in You.
Amen.
